description:
This role is for one of Weekday's clients. 
 Location: Remote
 Employment Type: Independent Contractor
 Compensation: USD 50–120 per hour
 About the Role
 We are seeking experienced GPU Programming Software Engineers to contribute to an AI training and development project focused on GPU architecture, performance optimization, and high-performance computing.
 In this role, you will leverage your GPU programming expertise to design, develop, test, and optimize GPU-based tasks that help train and improve Large Language Models (LLMs). You will work with GPU programming technologies such as CUDA, WebGPU, and GLSL to build efficient kernels and shaders, improve computational performance, and develop reliable software solutions.
 This opportunity is ideal for engineers with strong programming fundamentals and hands-on experience in GPU computing, graphics programming, machine learning acceleration, or scientific computing.
 Requirements 
 Key Responsibilities
 Design, develop, and optimize GPU-based software solutions using CUDA, WebGPU, GLSL, or other relevant GPU programming technologies.
 Create and implement GPU programming tasks and workflows to support LLM training and evaluation.
 Profile, benchmark, and fine-tune GPU kernels and shaders to maximize performance and computational efficiency.
 Identify performance bottlenecks and implement optimization techniques for GPU workloads.
 Develop host-side logic, interfaces, and integrations using C++.
 Evaluate GPU implementations for correctness, scalability, and performance.
 Document technical approaches, implementation details, and optimization outcomes.
 Ensure completed tasks meet defined technical specifications and quality standards.
 Required Qualifications
 Advanced hands-on experience with at least one GPU programming language or framework capable of running on NVIDIA GPUs.
 Strong understanding of GPU architecture, parallel computing, and performance optimization.
 Proficiency in C++ and experience developing host-side applications or integrations.
 Ability to design, implement, debug, and optimize GPU-based programs.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Ability to work independently and deliver high-quality technical outputs within project deadlines.
 Preferred Background
 Candidates with experience in one or more of the following domains are particularly encouraged to apply:
 Graphics Programming
 Machine Learning Acceleration
 Scientific Computing
 High-Performance Computing (HPC)
 GPU Kernel Development
 Parallel Computing
 Computer Architecture
 Relevant Technologies
 CUDA
 WebGPU
 GLSL
 C++
 NVIDIA GPU Architecture
 GPU Kernels and Shaders
 Performance Profiling and Benchmarking
 Parallel Programming and Optimization
 Compensation Structure
 Compensation ranges from USD 50–120 per hour .
 Payment is output-based, with experts compensated for tasks that successfully meet the specified project requirements.
 Task completion time may vary depending on complexity, technical expertise, and individual workflow.
 Minimum submission requirements apply, and contractors are expected to complete and submit a minimum number of tasks each week.
 Start Timeline & Availability
 Positions are typically filled within 48 hours.
 Candidates should be available to begin immediately.
 Selected candidates are expected to start their first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.
 Ideal Candidate: A skilled GPU programming engineer with advanced knowledge of GPU technologies, strong C++ proficiency, and practical experience building and optimizing high-performance GPU applications. The ideal candidate can independently deliver efficient, reliable, and technically accurate solutions.
